In the 136th episode of #MannKiBaat, PM @narendramodi shared that:

✅ The Kargil Vijay Diwas today fills us with pride and reminds us of the extraordinary courage of our brave soldiers.

✅ Global confidence in India’s defence equipment and technology is growing. Earlier this month, a major agreement regarding BrahMos and Astra missiles was concluded with Indonesia.

✅ Vikram-1, India's first rocket developed by the private sector, was launched last Sunday. This is the result of opening of the Space sector to private enterprise, allowing youngsters to show their talent.

✅ The Indian contingent delivered a spectacular performance in Science Olympiads, winning medals in all the Physics, Chemistry, Biology & Mathematics Olympiads.

✅ Ronaldo Laishram, an astrophysicist from Manipur, works in Japan and has been part of the team that discovered a massive cluster of young galaxies. Ronaldo named it ‘Loktak Proto cluster’, linking it to Manipur’s freshwater lake.

✅ Indians extend their best wishes to the Indian contingent participating at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, which began a few days ago.

✅ India won the first-ever women’s test match at Lord’s cricket ground, defeating England by 270 runs. Also, shuttler P.V. Sindhu scripted history by becoming the first Indian to win the Japan Open.

What a maddening final.

First takeaway: I should have converted one of those four match points. That’s one I’ll think about for a while.

Second takeaway: I don’t think Chen’s radar was fully dialed in today. There were a few too many uncharacteristic errors, especially around the sidelines. Against a player like Akane, that margin for error simply doesn’t exist.

One moment that really stood out was game point, when Akane turned down the shuttle change. It tells you just how much the drift was on both players’ minds. On the faster end, the last thing you want is an even quicker shuttle. It was a small moment that perfectly captured just how drifty the conditions were throughout the final.

And my two cents… on her day, Akane is borderline unplayable. One of the most skillful players our sport has ever seen, and a thoroughly deserving champion. Congratulations, Akane👏🏸

My performance in the last few events has been quite disappointing, not just for me, but for all of you who support me.

In order to find my best form my team and I have decided that I should compete with slightly less intensity over the next few months. Consequently, we feel it is in my best interest to skip long events away from home to allow for more dedicated training time.

With this in mind, I approached the Grand Chess Tour organizers and asked to play only two European Rapid & Blitz events. They were very supportive and understanding, and we agreed that I would participate in the Rapid & Blitz tournaments in Warsaw and Zagreb this year. I’m very grateful for their support. Respectfully, I am not planning to play any other events during the Grand Chess Tour schedule and will certainly be back for the full Grand Chess Tour in the future".
